paragraphs: Friend, here's the heart of this passage. Jesus knows exactly what's ahead. He tells the Twelve that He will be mocked, flogged and killed, and that "on the third day He will rise again" (Luke 18:33). He walks toward Jerusalem anyway, and that is the love of the Son of Man, who came to give His life to rescue people (Mark 10:45).

The disciples didn't understand it, because "the meaning was hidden from them" (Luke 18:34). And a man who couldn't see a thing understood who Jesus was. He called Him "Son of David," and he asked for mercy (Luke 18:38). Friend, I can't explain that one, but I love it. You don't need to have it all figured out to cry out to Jesus.

So when the crowd says hush, you get LOUDER, baker. Jesus stopped for that man, and He asked, "What do you want Me to do for you?" (Luke 18:41). He still welcomes people who come to Him with an honest ask. The man followed Jesus, glorifying God, and everyone who saw it gave praise to God (Luke 18:43), so ask Him boldly and give Him the glory.
